post.caption: Pliny said one knot heals wounds faster. It is called the Hercules knot, or the Herakles knot, and Greek goldsmiths tied it into gold diadems and bracelets. It was popular in jewelry by the 300s BCE, and a British Museum diadem with this knot is over 2,300 years old. Legend says Hercules knotted the paws of his lion skin. The Met says its popularity suggests a charm against evil. A Roman writer says brides wore a wool belt with this knot, and the groom untied it, which was meant as a good omen. Pliny wrote about it nearly 2,000 years ago.
